title: Refunds of Duplicate Payments on TRICARE Prime Installments
content:
A refund is owed when an installment of a fee-bearing **TRICARE Prime** enrollment whose status is applied or active has been paid more than once. A duplicate on the first installment charge - the installment charge whose coverage period begins on the enrollment's effective date - of an enrollment that took effect in the current plan year is not settled under this rule.

## Effect of issuing the refund

- One refund is added to the enrollment's fee account against the payment named.
- It goes back through the same payment method that payment used and carries today's posting date.
- The enrollment's fee balance owed rises by the amount refunded, and the refund shows on the fee account against that payment.

## Invocation

The tool is `refund_duplicate_payment_360f0d4a`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it for the verified caller.

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `related_fee_entry_id` | the reference number of the payment being refunded, read from the fee-account lookup for the enrollment - a payment entry, not the installment charge | identifier, as returned |
| `amount` | the amount refunded | US dollars, a plain number with 2 decimal places (cents, rounded half up), 0.00 or more |

## Return

On success: `refunded` (true when the refund was added), `prime_fee_entry_id` (the refund's reference number, beginning "pfr"), `related_fee_entry_id` (the payment refunded), `payment_method` (the method the refund goes back through, copied from that payment), `amount` (USD, 2 decimals) and `fee_balance_due` (the enrollment's fee balance owed after the refund, USD, 2 decimals; a negative figure is a credit owed to the beneficiary). No other outcome is defined.

## Contract questions

**Is the refund posted against the installment charge?** No. The reference given is the payment's own reference number; the refund stands against that payment.

**Can the refund go back by a method chosen at the call?** No parameter carries a method; the refund follows the method of the payment named.
